Maintenance Report — MNT-0144-003

Asset: WELL-0144 (NE-07 Well 144, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: flowline Work started: 27 Jan 2023 08:00 · Finished: 27 Jan 2023 21:00 · Well stopped for this job: 13 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Brian Coleman · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0144-0014 on 2023-01-26 Report written: 28 Jan 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0144-0014 at 11:45 on 2023-01-26 found crude oil on the pad: about 11.1% of the pad area, estimated 1.9 bbl. The inspector noted: "Staining along flowline route." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 7.2 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a corrosion hole along the flowline route.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 3 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak point.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in new line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 348 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 278 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 3.9 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0144-003 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.28% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0144-013

Asset: WELL-0144 (NE-07 Well 144, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 31 Aug 2024 08:00 · Finished: 04 Sep 2024 04:00 · Well stopped for this job: 92 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Daniel Foster Triggered by: inspection INS-0144-0097 on 2024-08-29 Report written: 05 Sep 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the motor breaker kept tripping and the pump jack would not run. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0144-0097 showed the wellhead at 40.8 °C with the air at 35.2 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 2 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Moisture got into the motor terminal box and damaged the windings.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 4 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.
